questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to experience uni in the UK, great city plus the highlands and Erasmus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Almost an overload of information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My student advisor

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think everybody who wanted university accommodation got it. Just remember to check your UoE mail and be patient. It is quite difficult but not impossible to find something through spareroom/Facebook. Your initial picks when you apply don't matter it all. Furthermore, you will most likely end up in a post grad student accommodation since most since most danish students are a couple of years older than local students, so don't worry about ending up with 17/18 year old freshers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everyone lives off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Buy a mattress topper!!! It really improved my springy bed and costed around 30 pounds. And if you get a poorly located accommodation you can probably change it by calling them after arrival. However, most I knew including myself got a pretty nicely located dorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as pretty easy. You upload a prioritized list of ten courses with your application and finalize it in July, but there is still plenty of time to change if you regret after you arrive. Just talk to your student advisor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student advisor after arrival and a CSE email that responded pretty quickly in the summer

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got my 1st, 3rd and 4th priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it if you're a science student. I heard from friends who did humanities that it for them is more difficult.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the level is around the same, but the workload was a little higher during the semester. This is also because one of my courses did not have a final exam and therefore had a larger amount of in course assessment.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Lectures were quite similar except in SFP3 where a lot of the lectures were flipped learning. 
There were more focus on general learning among the students and less on the final exam which was very nice.
The tutorials with theoretical exercises were more class based like high school and less where you just get a bunch of assignments and then TA's walk around and help like at UCPH. There were also way more graded in course assessment hence the weight of the final exam was less. In one of my courses, I had already passed the course before my exam.
And the lab sessions are significantly less independent! Sometimes it really felt like being a TV chef or something which made them quite easy and cosy, but not that educational.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology 3, Structures and functions of proteins 3 and Pharmacology 3

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked all my courses.
I probably learned the most from Structures and functions of proteins 3, but it was also pretty high demand with a lot of assessments. Just be aware of this and remember there is no grade pressure on you as an exchange student so focus on learning!
Immunology 3 and pharmacology 3 were both very interesting and required less work. The course organizers in immunology were fantastic.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's quite expensive to buy all the stuff needed when moving into a student accommodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping (lidl) was quite cheap. Book shops were everywhere and books were very cheap compared to DK. Museums were free. Beers at pubs could vary quite a lot but a lot of places give student discounts so remember your card. You also just live less frugally than at home, so even though everything except housing is cheaper then save up/apply for grants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The hillwalking club is great and gives you the opportunity to go on pretty hardcore hikes at remote places with only a few other people. I definitely recommend if you wanna hike and you'll meet some very nice people.
Also joining another sport you find interesting is a very nice way to meet and befriend locals. This was the main way for me at least.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes with the hillwalking club, in general explore the highlands and other scottish cities. Also remember to socialize in the weekends and go to the pubs and party! Don't spend your weekends studying any more than necessary.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sports clubs or societies. This is definitely the easiest way. You can also ask people from your study groups as there is quite a lot of group work at the school of biology.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and inclusiveness of the locals. It is much more easy meeting people you don't know than in Copenhagen. Also just the pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't worry too much about all the practical stuff. It's gonna work out all fine.
Be openminded and try out new things. Go a bit out of your comfort zone in the beginning, but also remember you'll be there for a long time and that friendships are not necessarily made in the first week.
Become a regular at a place or 2. It gives a very nice sense of belonging.
And explore the highlands!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for the grants which you can only apply for from September. A lot of other exchange students get excluded from this since their exchange begin in august. Also the weather was way better than expected.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Establishing an everyday life in a new country and all the great people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The intense socializing with a lot of new people in the beginning. This was pretty demanding

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go!!!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
